projects.name: Strengthen social protection and response structures for improved access to inclusive, gender related information and services for women, youth and girls, particularly marginalized groups
projects.description:
UN Women will strengthen social protection and response structures by expanding access to information, improving service delivery, and enhancing real-time responsiveness for marginalized and digitally excluded populations. User-friendly digital tools such as Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) and Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems would be employed to scale the use of mobile phone communication (analog phone) accessible by members of rural communities. By embedding this element into a local government service delivery framework, the initiative would seek to bridge the gap between policy and practice, ensuring no one is left behind to achieve protection, dignity and equal opportunity. This would also aid understanding of national policies and cultural appropriate information and foster access to information in local dialects.

The project will further Strengthen Community-Based referrals and Redress Mechanisms for Gender-Based Violence (GBV) through the development of strong community-based redress mechanisms to address discrimination, violence, and non-compliance with gender laws, responding to GBV issues especially for marginalized groups in the local communities. The project will leverage existing community structures to serve as safe homes through rehabilitation, coordination and logistical support for effective and efficient service delivery to SGBV victims, while simultaneously carrying out a study on best practices and developing a business case for sustainability of safe spaces in Sierra Leone.

projects.name: The institutional capacity of local councils and key Ministries Department and Agencies (MDAs) strengthened to effectively deliver inclusive and gender-sensitive services that uphold the leave no one behind (LNOB) principles for underserved communities
projects.description:
Under this output, the project will scale up investment in the five piloted local councils and one additional district to further strengthen their capacities in gender mainstreaming across development planning, monitoring, and implementation. The planned scale-up of gender-responsive budgeting (GRB) capacity is both timely and aligned with ongoing national efforts. While pilot Ministries Department and Agencies (MDAs) are already operating under GRB obligations and some local councils have undertaken gender-budget analyses, implementation at the local level remains inconsistent and limited. The project’s support, comprising web-based monitoring and reporting platform, training, tools, mentorship, and peer learning, will therefore be critical in helping councils institutionalize GRB practices and achieve more inclusive, gender-sensitive resource allocation. The Minister of Gender has expressed a strong need to strengthen the capacity of ministry staff to effectively implement national laws, including the GEWE Act 2022 and related legislation, to ensure professional, consistent, and gender-responsive service delivery across all levels. The local councils and key Ministry staff require structured training, practical tools, and opportunities for peer learning to operationalize gender-responsive governance, planning, budgeting, service delivery, monitoring, and advocacy.
Building on existing gains, the project will equip staff on key gender related topics and resource mobilization strategies, including proposal writing, donor engagement, and public-private partnerships and leverage innovative tools, partnerships and develop accredited training modules building on the induction manuals created by UN Women and UNICEF for the Ministry of Gender and Children’s Affairs (MOGCA). Standardized toolkits, peer learning exchanges, and technical mentorship will enable rapid replication and adaptation of gender-responsive practices across councils. Priority areas include Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Harassment (PSEA/H), GBV protection protocols, disability, child protection, advocacy, communication, leadership and governance skills.
Additionally, the project will strengthen monitoring, reporting, and accountability mechanisms by establishing a decentralized web-based Monitoring, Evaluation and accountability platform with user-friendly dashboards, real-time data collection, and interoperability. This will be aligned with the National Monitoring and Evaluation Authority (NaMEA) and integrated existing national systems. Using the UN Results-Based Management approach, the project will integrate gender-responsive indicators and adaptive monitoring into local and national planning processes.This will improve the availability and use of disaggregated data, including sex, age, and disability, for evidence-based decision-making.
The project will also build on existing work by development partners such as the World Bank and UNDP, which have supported local governance reforms and M&E strengthening. Lessons from their performance assessment systems, digital tools, and capacity-building initiatives will be incorporated to reinforce complementarities, avoid duplication, and accelerate the adoption of transparent and gender-responsive M&E practices across councils and ministries.

projects.name: Comprehensive beneficiary mobilization methodology developed, operationalized to facilitate beneficiary selection for inclusive job creation for youth and women in climate-smart agriculture value chains and waste management.
projects.description:
This methodology outlines a structured, inclusive, and participatory approach to identify, verify, and prepare Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and Male Champions as project beneficiaries across Sierra Leone’s Southern, Eastern, and Western Area regions. The strategy prioritizes transparency, gender equity, Environmental and Social (E&S) Considerations with a strong cost efficiency approach and focus on engaging women- and youth-led enterprises. UN Women will employ evidenced based approach, levering on existing top-performing MSMES and cooperatives data bases to participate in the selection process. Clear criteria and standardized screening forms are established to identify, assess, and verify candidates for participation in the project. Mobilize women, youth, and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises as beneficiaries of the WOKDONCAM Project according to the project appraisal report will include;
1. To identify, verify, and mobilize beneficiaries engaged in agriculture, fisheries, and waste management within the designated project locations.
2. To compile and submit a list of qualified potential beneficiaries for consideration and approval by the project team.
3. To conduct awareness-raising activities targeting beneficiaries and local authorities to ensure understanding and support for the project.
4. To inform beneficiaries of training logistics, including date, venue, and participant allocation per enterprise, group, or association, in alignment with the program’s training schedule.
5. To identify and engage male champions at the community level who will advocate for women’s economic empowerment.
